chapter: New York, the Lafayette and the Cotton Club
title: Joe Jones's outburst at the West End bar
summary: Crawford recalls Joe Jones grabbing his arm when he sat in, and Jones shouting at Matthew Gee for walking in front of him.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: No, sir. Owney Madden I think I saw once or twice. Mike Bess, he was the other partner. Herman Starks -- so I didn't know. Back to Joe Jones -- my wife and I were sitting listening to the group that was playing there, and Joe finished his solo.
This is at the West End Bar?

Yeah. Joe had finished his solo, and he went in the back. Naturally, wrapped himself in a towel around his neck like he -- a prize fighter or something and wouldn't -- sat in the back, way back there somewhere. And so I enjoyed his solo, so I -- was going to -- I'm retired now. I just wanted to see how my hands felt on the drum. He sat in on my drums many times.

And I sat down and started doing some of his things, da-dump-tee-tee-tee, ka-ka-kuh, you know, that kind of stuff, that old (inaudible), and Joe ran up there and grabbed my arm and tried to pull it out of the socket. Don't do that. Get down. Don't do that, friendly as we are.

I politely got up, told my wife, come on, baby, let's go. I got out of there. While he was playing his solo, though, Matthew Gee Jean walked in front of him on the bandstand. He was only (inaudible). And Joe screamed bloody murder at Matthew Gee Jean. If this was Buddy Rich, you wouldn't walk in front of him. I said, what the hell is that. That man said -- why did he say that? If this was Buddy Rich, you wouldn't walk in front of him.
I got so mad with that bum then.

That was before he tried to pull my arm out of the socket. I just kept quiet. (inaudible) just keep quiet. And so I didn't say anything to him. Matthew didn't say anything to him, just (inaudible) stand up against the wall. He had to get over there in his position. Well, I don't know why Matthew walked in front of him.

But the -- I asked Matthew about it later when he was up here, came up here. I said, I wonder why Joe would make a statement like that? He said, oh, man, don't pay him no mind. He's got a loose screw. Everybody knows he's got a loose screw (inaudible) or something like that, said, we don't even speak.
Now, going back to Cotton Club. Now,
